name: Thirst is granted by spells that cost health (#1852)
contract: Issue #1852 was filed on Thirst 500107, which no acquisition table grants; the obtainable Thirst is 92112 (CharacterAdvancement.dbc row 4025, class 20, plus the live-client capture). 92112's tooltip is 'Spells that cost health now grant Thirst.' Its effect 0 is SPELL_AURA_PROC_TRIGGER_SPELL (aura 42) on Thirst 706613, the Blood thirst resource of AscensionCustomResourceData.h:58, StackAmount 10, DurationIndex 18 = 20 s; effect 1 is aura 149 SPELL_AURA_REDUCE_PUSHBACK and is native. Spell.dbc gives 92112 ProcFlags 0 and no spell_proc row existed, so SpellMgr::LoadSpellProcs generated no entry, SpellMgr::GetSpellProcEntry returned nullptr and Aura::GetProcEffectMask returned 0; no ResourceGainRule names 706613 either, so no Bloodmage could ever earn a stack. The probe is Bloodmoon Blast 572332, the rank a level-80 character owns: family 26, DmgClass 1 (magic), harmful, PowerType -2 (POWER_HEALTH) with ManaCostPercentage 7 and no cooldown, so every cast raises PROC_FLAG_DONE_SPELL_MAGIC_DMG_CLASS_NEG at PROC_SPELL_PHASE_CAST and satisfies PROC_ATTR_REQ_MANA_COST. The control is Sanguine Mend 504086: also family 26 and DmgClass 1 but positive, so it raises PROC_FLAG_DONE_SPELL_MAGIC_DMG_CLASS_POS, which the same spell_proc row also carries, and it declares ManaCost 200 so it passes PROC_ATTR_REQ_MANA_COST too - its only difference is PowerType 1 (Rage). It therefore isolates the one condition no spell_proc column expresses, the POWER_HEALTH test in aura_ascension_bloodmage_thirst. The tooltip's second sentence, 'Reaching 10 stacks makes you Insatiable', has no effect slot in 92112 and no record casts Insatiable 706621 on a stack threshold, so it is not asserted here.

steps.label: Let spawn AI and level scaling settle
Cast time 2000 ms plus the proc window
Control: without the passive a health-cost cast grants no Thirst
Cast time 2500 ms plus the proc window
Control: a Rage-cost Bloodmage spell grants no Thirst even with the passive
DISCRIMINATING: a health-cost cast now grants one stack of Thirst
Each further health-cost cast adds a stack
